md_description: Workflow for generating single amplified genome datasets from archaeal communities collected at extreme environmental sites such as hydrothermal vents. The pipeline covers sample collection, lysis, isothermal amplification, high-throughput sequencing, and computational genome assembly to produce sequencing-derived genomic outputs for studying archaeal adaptation to extreme conditions and their biochemical roles in the ecosystem.

archaeal_community_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic sample identity and provenance fields: where the archaeal community sample came from, what extreme environment it was collected from, and the environmental conditions at collection. I excluded any lysis, amplification, sequencing, or computational fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any sample/subject/experiment identifiers if they had already been generated elsewhere; since none were provided in already_generated here, I kept the schema focused on origin and collection conditions only. Fields are framed to support reuse and interpretation of the sample without describing what was done to it.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the field-collected archaeal community sample; use a stable string such as 'SAG_vent_001'. This is assigned at the root entity level and should identify the sample across all downstream workflow steps.

Name of the sampling location where the archaeal community was obtained, such as a hydrothermal vent field, hot spring, or other extreme environmental site. Record the site name as used in field notes or expedition metadata.
Broad environmental category of the sample origin at collection. Use this to distinguish extreme habitat types relevant to archaeal ecology.
Latitude of the sample collection location in decimal degrees at the time of sampling; typical range -90 to 90. Record the georeferenced field site position, not a laboratory location.
Longitude of the sample collection location in decimal degrees at the time of sampling; typical range -180 to 180. Record the georeferenced field site position, not a laboratory location.
Sampling depth at collection in meters, measured at the site of origin. Use 0 for surface collections and positive values for water-column, vent, or subsurface sampling where applicable.

In situ temperature of the source environment at the time of sample collection, in degrees Celsius. Typical range for extreme archaeal habitats may span about 0 to 120+; record the field measurement or best available site estimate.
In situ pH of the sample environment at collection. Typical range 0 to 14; record the field measurement or site estimate for the archaeal habitat.

Salinity of the source environment at collection, in practical salinity units (PSU) or equivalent field estimate. Use this for hypersaline or marine extreme habitats; typical range is approximately 0 to 300+ depending on site.
Date when the archaeal community sample was collected in the field, recorded as the sampling date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).

Brief description of how the environmental sample was obtained from the site, for example vent fluid filtration, sediment coring, or water collection. Keep this at the sample provenance level, not the downstream processing level.
Physical material type collected from the environment, such as water, sediment, biofilm, or vent fluid-associated particulate material. This describes the sample itself at intake.

cell_lysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the operational parameters of the lysis step: the disruption method, key reagent/kit details, mechanical/chemical settings, duration, temperature, and a simple post-lysis quality indicator. I excluded sample origin and collection properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded amplified DNA properties because those belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided duplicating any fields already generated for the sample node, since this process should describe how lysis was performed rather than what the sample is. No agent/software fields were added here because the process agent is already specified in the DAG as researcher and the core requirement is the lysis protocol itself.

md_schema.descr: Primary disruption approach used to lyse archaeal cells and release nucleic acids, recorded at the lysis step before amplification. Examples include mechanical bead beating, thermal lysis, detergent-based lysis, enzymatic lysis, or combined methods.

Commercial kit, reagent system, or custom lysis reagent set used for cell disruption, recorded at the point of the lysis protocol. Use the exact product name when applicable, for example a vendor kit or custom buffer formulation.

Concentration of the principal lysis reagent used in the protocol, measured at the lysis step. Use the assay-relevant unit embedded in the value description, for example percent v/v, percent w/v, mg_per_ml, or mmol_per_l as appropriate for the reagent used.

Temperature at which the cell lysis reaction was performed, in degrees Celsius. Typical range may include about 0 to 100 depending on the protocol; record the actual incubation temperature used during disruption.
Total duration of the lysis incubation or mechanical disruption phase, in minutes. Record the elapsed time used for cell disruption before nucleic acid recovery proceeds.

Operational setting for any mechanical disruption applied during lysis, such as bead-beating speed, cycle count, or pulse duration. Record the primary setting value used in the protocol at the lysis step.

Simple quality indicator for the lysed material immediately after lysis, such as visible disruption, turbidity change, or estimated nucleic acid release. Use this as a brief process outcome indicator, not a quantified DNA measurement.

lysed_cell_material.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the lysed material itself: its identity as a post-lysis material, whether it was retained as a liquid or pellet/resuspension, and basic DNA-bearing material quality attributes that describe the entity rather than the lysis process or amplification outcome. I excluded lysis protocol settings because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded any amplification input conditions or sequencing-related properties because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating the sample provenance fields already generated for the root sample entity; this node describes the material produced by lysis, not where the sample came from. The fields are intentionally minimal but sufficient for a downstream user to know what form of material entered amplification.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the material obtained immediately after cell lysis; use a stable string such as 'LYS_001'. This identifies the post-lysis entity that is carried into the amplification step.

Physical state of the lysed cell material immediately after lysis and before amplification, for example whether it remained as a suspension, pellet, or extracted lysate. Record the observed state at the handoff between lysis and amplification.

Qualitative amount of residual visible cellular debris in the lysed material after lysis and prior to amplification. Use this as a coarse description of material cleanliness at the entity level, not as a downstream QC metric.

Indicator of whether genomic DNA presence was confirmed in the lysed material before amplification, based on the workflow's pre-amplification check if performed. This describes the material's suitability for amplification, not the amplification process itself.

Overall assessment of whether the lysed material was deemed suitable for downstream amplification at the point of transfer. Use this to capture whether the material was acceptable, borderline, or not suitable for the next step.

isothermal_amplification.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the isothermal amplification was performed: the amplification method, kit or chemistry, reaction temperature and duration, reaction volume, input DNA amount, and a basic amplification success indicator. I excluded the properties of the lysed input material because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded amplified DNA characteristics because those belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided any sequencing or assembly fields, since those are outside the amplification step. Because the DAG explicitly assigns a researcher agent here, I did not add agent metadata fields; instead I focused on protocol-operational details needed to reproduce the amplification step.

md_schema.descr: Isothermal amplification strategy used to amplify released archaeal DNA at this process step, recorded before sequencing library preparation. Examples include multiple displacement amplification or other whole-genome/single-cell isothermal approaches.
Commercial kit, vendor chemistry, or custom reagent set used for the isothermal amplification reaction. Record the exact product name or formulation used at the amplification step.
Total reaction volume of the isothermal amplification mix in microliters, measured at setup. Typical values are often in the low tens of microliters; record the actual volume used.

Amount of lysed-cell DNA input added to the amplification reaction, in nanograms, measured at the time the reaction was assembled. Typical range may be trace to low-ng amounts for single-cell or low-input workflows.

Incubation temperature used for isothermal amplification, in degrees Celsius. Typical range depends on chemistry but is often around 30 to 42; record the actual temperature used during the amplification reaction.
Total incubation time for the isothermal amplification reaction, in hours. Record the elapsed amplification time from reaction start to termination.

Number of repeated incubation or amplification cycles used if the protocol includes discrete cycling or repeated reaction phases. Use 1 when the amplification is a single continuous incubation without cycles.
Indicator of whether the amplification reaction produced usable amplified DNA at the end of the process step. This is a simple process-level outcome, not a property of the product entity.

amplified_genomic_dna.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only properties intrinsic to the amplified DNA product: its identity, what amplification chemistry generated it, approximate fragment size distribution, yield, and basic purity/integrity indicators that describe the material itself. I excluded the amplification protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded library preparation and sequencing properties because those belong downstream. I also avoided reusing the upstream sample or lysed material provenance fields, since this node represents the product of amplification rather than the original specimen. The selected fields give downstream users enough information to judge whether the amplified DNA is suitable for library preparation and comparative reuse.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the amplified DNA product generated from the lysed material; use a stable string such as 'AMP_DNA_001'. This identifies the amplified DNA entity that enters sequencing library preparation.

High-level classification of the amplified DNA product at the entity level, for example whole-genome amplified DNA or single-cell amplified DNA. Record the product category that best matches the output of the amplification step.

Measured concentration of the amplified DNA product after amplification and before library preparation, in nanograms per microliter. Typical values may vary widely across single-cell workflows; record the quantified concentration used for downstream input assessment.
Total mass of amplified DNA recovered from the amplification reaction, in nanograms. Record the yield as measured on the amplified DNA entity before it is handed off to library preparation.

Approximate mean fragment size of the amplified DNA product, in base pairs, measured after amplification and before sequencing library preparation. Use this as a summary of the amplified DNA size distribution.

A260/A280 purity ratio for the amplified DNA product, measured after amplification and before library preparation. Typical values near 1.8 indicate relatively pure DNA; record the observed ratio if measured.

Qualitative assessment of amplification bias or uneven genome coverage expected from the amplified DNA product. Use this entity-level indicator to flag whether the amplified DNA appears low-bias, moderate-bias, or high-bias for downstream sequencing use.

sequencing_library_prep.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the operational details of how the sequencing library was prepared from amplified DNA: the library preparation kit or chemistry, fragmentation/tagmentation approach, input mass, target insert size, adapter/indexing scheme, PCR enrichment cycles, and a simple prep success indicator. I excluded amplified DNA properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded library product attributes such as file-like outputs or sequencing read properties because those belong to the downstream Entity/Signal nodes. I also avoided duplicating any fields already generated for amplification or the sample, focusing only on the protocol used to convert amplified DNA into a sequencing-ready library. The field set is sufficient for reproducing the library prep step and understanding compatibility with the downstream sequencer.

md_schema.descr: Commercial kit, reagent system, or custom protocol used to convert amplified genomic DNA into a sequencing library. Record the exact kit or chemistry used at the library preparation step.

Method used to fragment or tagment the amplified DNA during library preparation, recorded at the library prep step. Examples include enzymatic fragmentation, mechanical shearing, or transposase-based tagmentation.
Amount of amplified genomic DNA input used to start the library preparation reaction, in nanograms. Record the mass actually loaded into the prep reaction before adapter addition and enrichment.

Intended insert size of the prepared library fragments, in base pairs, established during library preparation. Typical values depend on platform and protocol; record the target size chosen for this workflow.

Adapter and indexing strategy used during library preparation, such as single-index, dual-index, or unique dual-index designs. Record the scheme applied to the sequencing library before capture on the sequencer.
Number of PCR enrichment cycles performed during library preparation, measured at the library prep step. Use 0 if no amplification PCR was used after adapter ligation or tagmentation.

Indicator of whether the library preparation step produced a sequencing-ready library suitable for loading onto the platform. This is a process-level outcome, not a property of the library file or sequencing reads.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared sequencing library: its identity, library molecule concentration, average insert size, adapter/index composition, library complexity, and whether it passed pre-sequencing QC. I excluded the library preparation protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded sequencer configuration and read/file properties because those belong downstream to the Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating the amplified DNA input fields already defined upstream. These fields are enough for a downstream user to understand what library was loaded into the sequencer and whether it was fit for capture.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library; use a stable string such as 'LIB_001'. This identifies the library entity that is loaded onto the sequencing instrument.

Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library in nanograms per microliter, determined after library prep and before sequencing load. Typical values depend on the platform and cleanup method; record the quantified concentration used for loading decisions.
Average insert size of the prepared library molecules in base pairs, measured after library preparation and before sequencing. Use this as the representative fragment length of the library entity.

Description of the adapter and index sequences present in the prepared library molecules, recorded as an entity attribute before sequencing. Use this to capture the indexing design carried by the library.

Qualitative or semi-quantitative estimate of the diversity of unique library molecules available for sequencing at the entity stage. Record whether the library is expected to be low, moderate, or high complexity based on pre-sequencing assessment.

Indicator of whether the prepared sequencing library passed the pre-sequencing quality control check and was deemed suitable for loading onto the sequencer. This describes the entity's readiness for capture, not the QC assay itself.

high_throughput_sequencing.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration used to generate the raw sequencing data: platform name, manufacturer, instrument model, serial number, run/flow cell identifiers, read structure settings, chemistry/kit, and key run conditions controlled by the operator. I excluded sample, library, and read/file properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes or the downstream Signal node. I also avoided adding any computational or interpretive fields, since capture metadata should describe how the instrument was configured rather than what the output means. The DAG already specifies a high-throughput sequencer agent, so I focused on the specific instrument and run settings needed to reproduce the capture event.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the high-throughput sequencing instrument used to generate the raw reads, recorded at the capture step. Examples include Illumina, Thermo Fisher, or equivalent platform vendors.
Instrument model used for the sequencing run, recorded at the capture step. Use the exact model name and, if applicable, platform designation such as NovaSeq, HiSeq, or equivalent.

Serial number or other unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used for capture. Record the exact instrument identifier as configured for the run, for example a vendor serial number string.

Unique identifier for the sequencing session or run that produced the raw read data. Use a stable string such as a run accession or instrument run name to link the capture event to the downstream FASTQ output.
Identifier of the flow cell or sequencing consumable used during the capture session, recorded at run setup. This should match the specific flow cell loaded on the instrument for the sequencing run.
Sequencing chemistry or kit version used on the instrument during capture, such as the vendor chemistry relevant to the chosen platform. Record the exact chemistry associated with the run.
Configured read length in base pairs for each read generated by the sequencer at the capture step. Record the intended read length setting, for example 150 bp or 250 bp, before data generation.
Read structure used for sequencing capture, describing whether the run generated single-end or paired-end reads. Record the instrument configuration used for the raw read session.
Number of lanes or equivalent parallel partitions used during the sequencing run, if applicable to the platform. Record the instrument-run configuration used for the capture session.
Date on which the sequencing capture session was performed, recorded as the run date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).

Loading or clustering parameter used for the sequencing run, such as library loading concentration or resulting cluster density, measured at run setup or instrument pre-run metrics. Record the value appropriate to the platform used.

raw_sequence_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only technical properties of the raw FASTQ artefact itself: file identity, format, size, read count, read lengths, base-quality summaries, compression status, and storage location. I excluded instrument settings and run conditions because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded any preprocessing or assembly interpretation because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating library or sample metadata already defined upstream. The selected fields are sufficient for data management, integrity checking, and reuse of the raw sequencing output.

md_schema.descr: File name of the raw sequencing reads artifact produced directly by the instrument, typically a FASTQ or FASTQ.GZ file. Record the exact filename used in storage or transfer.
Technical file format of the raw sequencing read artifact, recorded for the direct instrument output. Typical values are FASTQ or compressed FASTQ, as used for the raw read file.
Size of the raw sequencing reads file in bytes, measured after instrument output and before any preprocessing. This is a file property of the raw Signal artefact, not a scientific measurement.

Total number of reads contained in the raw sequencing output file, counted from the FASTQ records at the time of file generation or ingestion. Record the full read count before any trimming or filtering.

Observed read length in base pairs for the raw sequencing reads, typically corresponding to the configured output length of the instrument. Record the read length represented in the file at the raw Signal stage.
Mean base quality score across the raw sequencing reads, summarized from the FASTQ file before preprocessing. Use this as a technical quality metric for the raw data artefact.
Fraction of bases in the raw sequencing reads with quality score at or above Q30, measured on the raw FASTQ file. Use this as a standard technical quality summary of the Signal artefact.
Indicator of whether the raw sequencing output file is compressed, for example as gzipped FASTQ. This describes the technical storage state of the raw Signal artefact.
Path or URI where the raw sequencing reads file is stored, such as a local filesystem path, object storage URI, or repository location. Record the access location for the raw Signal artefact.

read_preprocessing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational operations used to transform raw reads into clean reads: the preprocessing software, its version, repository, trimming and filtering parameters, adapter handling, minimum length threshold, and a simple success indicator. I excluded raw-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded clean-read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided repeating sequencing instrument settings or assembly parameters, since preprocessing should describe the transformation logic rather than the measurement session or output artefact characteristics. Because the agent is bioinformatics software, software identity is important here and is included per the schema rules.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software tool used for read preprocessing, trimming, and filtering of the raw FASTQ data. Record the exact tool used at this process step, such as a read trimmer or quality filter.
Version of the preprocessing software used to clean raw reads before assembly. Record the exact version number or release tag so the process can be reproduced.

Repository, source, or package distribution associated with the preprocessing software used at this step. Record the code source or package location, such as a GitHub repository or package manager entry.
Indicator of whether adapter trimming was performed during preprocessing of the raw sequence reads. This records whether adapter sequences were explicitly removed before assembly.
Phred quality threshold used for trimming low-quality bases from raw reads during preprocessing. Typical values are often around 20 to 30; record the actual cutoff applied to the raw reads.
Minimum read length retained after preprocessing, in base pairs. Reads shorter than this threshold are discarded during cleaning; record the cutoff used before assembly.
Indicator of whether host or contaminant sequence filtering was applied during preprocessing of the raw reads. Use this to note any additional cleaning beyond adapter and quality trimming.
Indicator of whether the preprocessing step completed successfully and produced clean reads suitable for downstream assembly. This is a process-level outcome, not a property of the reads themselves.

clean_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only technical properties of the cleaned read artefact: file identity, format, size, read count, read lengths, quality summaries, retained read fraction, and storage location. I excluded preprocessing software and trimming parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded assembly or interpretation fields because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating raw-read properties beyond what is necessary to characterize the cleaned output itself. The fields are sufficient for tracking the cleaned dataset as a reusable intermediate signal for genome assembly.

md_schema.descr: File name of the cleaned read set produced after preprocessing, typically stored as FASTQ or FASTQ.GZ. Record the exact filename used for the assembly input signal.
Technical file format of the cleaned read artefact after preprocessing. Typical values are FASTQ or compressed FASTQ, matching the processed read file used for assembly.
Size of the cleaned reads file in bytes, measured after preprocessing and before assembly. This is a file property of the processed Signal artefact.
Total number of reads present in the cleaned read file after adapter removal and quality trimming. Record the count of retained reads that enter assembly.
Observed read length in base pairs for the cleaned reads after preprocessing. Record the representative length of the processed read set used for assembly.
Mean base quality score across the cleaned reads, calculated after preprocessing and before assembly. Use this as a technical quality summary for the Signal artefact.
Fraction of raw reads retained after preprocessing, calculated as cleaned reads divided by raw reads. Use this to summarize how much data remained in the processed read set before assembly.
Path or URI where the cleaned read file is stored, such as a filesystem location or object storage URI. Record the access location for the processed Signal artefact.

genome_assembly.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational assembly operations and software configuration: assembler name, version, repository, assembly strategy, parameterization, k-mer choices, and a basic assembly success indicator. I excluded clean-read properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded contig or draft genome properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided adding refinement or comparative-analysis fields, since those are separate downstream processes. Because the agent is assembly software, software identity is essential here and is included per the instructions.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to assemble the cleaned reads into contigs or draft genomes. Record the exact assembler tool used at this process step.
Version of the genome assembly software used for the assembly process. Record the exact version number or release tag so the assembly can be reproduced.
Repository, source, or package distribution associated with the assembly software used at this step. Record the code source or package location, such as a GitHub repository or package manager entry.
High-level assembly strategy used to generate draft contigs or genome drafts from cleaned reads. Examples include de novo assembly or co-assembly when multiple read sets are combined.

K-mer sizes used by the assembly software, recorded as a comma-separated string or equivalent text list at the assembly step. Use this field to capture the exact k-mer parameterization applied to the cleaned reads.
Minimum contig length retained or reported by the assembly process, in base pairs. Record the cutoff used to define contigs that are kept in the assembly output.
Expected or target genome size used as a guiding parameter during assembly, in megabases. Record this estimate if the assembler was configured with a size expectation or prior estimate.

Indicator of whether the assembly process completed successfully and produced contigs or draft genome output suitable for downstream refinement. This is a process-level outcome, not a property of the assembled derivative.

draft_genome_assembly.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed output properties of the draft assembly: the derivative identifier, number of contigs, total assembly length, N50, largest contig, GC content, completeness and contamination estimates, and a basic assembly quality flag. I excluded assembler parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded cleaned-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node. I also avoided downstream refinement or comparative-analysis fields, since this derivative is the assembly product before refinement. The selected fields are the minimum needed to evaluate the draft SAG as a reusable genomic result.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the draft genome assembly derivative; use a stable string such as 'DRAFT_ASM_001'. This identifies the assembled contig set produced from the cleaned reads.
Total number of contigs in the draft genome assembly, counted in the assembled output produced from the cleaned reads. Record the count at the derivative stage after assembly completion.
Sum of contig lengths in the draft genome assembly, in base pairs. Record the total assembled sequence length for the draft SAG derivative.

N50 statistic of the draft genome assembly, in base pairs, calculated from the contig length distribution after assembly. Use this standard assembly continuity metric to summarize the derivative quality.
Length of the largest contig in the draft genome assembly, in base pairs, measured on the assembled derivative output. This captures the longest contiguous sequence produced by assembly.
GC content of the draft genome assembly, expressed as a percentage of total assembled bases. Record the value computed from the assembled contigs at the derivative stage.
Estimated genome completeness of the draft assembly, expressed as a percentage. Use the completeness score available for the assembled derivative, typically from a genome-quality assessment tool.
Estimated contamination of the draft genome assembly, expressed as a percentage. Record the contamination estimate for the assembled derivative if it was assessed.

Overall quality assessment of the draft assembly derivative based on continuity, completeness, and contamination. Use this as a coarse summary of whether the draft SAG is acceptable for downstream refinement.

assembly_refinement.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational refinement operations applied to the draft assembly: the refinement software, version, repository, refinement strategy, contamination or binning thresholds, polishing rounds, and a success indicator. I excluded draft assembly properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the refined SAG properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating genome assembly parameters or comparative-analysis outputs, since refinement is a distinct post-assembly process. Because the agent is bioinformatics software, software identity is included to support reproducibility.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software tool used for assembly refinement, including binning, polishing, or contamination filtering. Record the exact tool used at this process step.
Version of the refinement software used to improve the draft genome assembly. Record the exact version number or release tag so the process can be reproduced.

Repository, source, or package distribution associated with the refinement software used at this step. Record the code source or package location, such as a GitHub repository or package manager entry.

Primary refinement strategy applied to the draft genome assembly, such as polishing, binning, contamination filtering, or a combination of these methods. Record the dominant post-assembly operation used for improvement.

Number of polishing iterations applied to the draft assembly during refinement, measured at the refinement step. Record the total number of polishing passes used if applicable; use 0 if no polishing was performed.

Contamination threshold used to retain or discard contigs or bins during refinement, expressed as a percentage. Record the cutoff applied when filtering likely contaminant sequences from the draft assembly.
Confidence or probability threshold used for bin assignment during refinement, if binning was part of the workflow. Record the cutoff used to accept contigs into a refined SAG bin.

Indicator of whether the assembly refinement step completed successfully and produced an improved genome derivative suitable for downstream analysis. This is a process-level outcome, not a property of the refined genome itself.

refined_sag.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed properties of the refined single amplified genome: its identity, final contig count and size, continuity metrics, completeness and contamination, taxonomy assignment, and an overall refinement quality flag. I excluded process parameters because those belong to the upstream refinement process, and I excluded downstream comparative-analysis outputs because those belong to the next derivative node. I also avoided repeating draft-assembly fields verbatim unless they are needed as final refined-output descriptors. These fields allow downstream users to assess the refined SAG as the stable genomic product entering comparative analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the refined single amplified genome derivative; use a stable string such as 'RSAG_001'. This identifies the final refined genome-level product used for downstream comparative analysis.
Total number of contigs remaining in the refined SAG after post-assembly refinement. Record the contig count for the final derivative genome product.
Total length of the refined SAG assembly in base pairs after refinement, calculated as the sum of remaining contigs. Record the final assembled genome size at the derivative stage.
N50 statistic of the refined SAG assembly, in base pairs, calculated after refinement. Use this as the final continuity metric for the refined derivative genome.
Estimated completeness of the refined SAG, expressed as a percentage after post-assembly refinement. Record the final genome completeness score for the derivative product.
Estimated contamination of the refined SAG, expressed as a percentage after post-assembly refinement. Record the final contamination score for the derivative product.

Taxonomic assignment of the refined SAG at the level available from the analysis workflow, such as domain, phylum, class, or genus. Record the final classification derived from the refined genome product.

Overall quality assessment of the refined SAG after refinement, based on completeness, contamination, and assembly continuity. Use this coarse flag to indicate whether the refined genome is suitable for downstream comparative analysis.

comparative_genome_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational analysis workflow used to interpret the refined SAGs: the analysis software, version, repository, analysis type, reference database, statistical thresholds, functional annotation source, and a success indicator. I excluded refined genome properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the final biological interpretation products because those belong to the downstream derivative node. I also avoided repeating assembly or refinement parameters, since comparative analysis is a distinct interpretation step. Because the agent is analysis software, software identity is included to support reproducibility of the inference stage.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software tool used for comparative genome analysis of the refined SAGs. Record the exact analysis package or pipeline used at this process step.
Version of the comparative genome analysis software used for the inference step. Record the exact version number or release tag so the analysis can be reproduced.
Repository, source, or package distribution associated with the analysis software used at this step. Record the code source or package location, such as a GitHub repository or package manager entry.

Primary type of comparative analysis performed on the refined SAGs, such as functional annotation, orthology comparison, pathway inference, or adaptive feature screening. Record the dominant analytical objective of this process step.

Name of the reference database or database collection used during comparative genome analysis, for example a protein family or pathway database. Record the exact resource consulted for annotation or comparison.

Primary statistical threshold used to accept hits, annotations, or comparative inferences in the analysis workflow, such as an e-value or probability cutoff. Record the main cutoff applied at this process step.

Source used to assign gene or pathway function during comparative analysis, such as a curated database or automated annotation pipeline. Record the main annotation source used to interpret the refined SAGs.

Indicator of whether the comparative genome analysis completed successfully and produced results suitable for interpretation. This is a process-level outcome, not a property of the analysis outputs themselves.

archaeal_adaptation_results.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed result properties from the comparative analysis: the result identifier, a concise adaptation signature summary, key functional categories or pathways inferred, confidence/score summaries, ecosystem role inference, and an overall result quality flag. I excluded software and statistical parameters because those belong to the upstream analysis process, and I excluded refined SAG properties because those belong to the upstream genome derivative. I also avoided sample provenance and sequencing details because they are outside the analytical result node. These fields are sufficient for downstream users to interpret and filter the final biological conclusions of the workflow.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final analytical results derivative; use a stable string such as 'ADAPT_001'. This identifies the output object containing the archaeal adaptation and ecosystem-function inferences.

Concise textual summary of the main archaeal adaptation signatures inferred from the comparative analysis, such as stress tolerance, energy metabolism, or environmental resilience features. Record the final interpretation produced by the analysis derivative.

List or summary of the major functional categories recovered in the final analysis, such as membrane adaptation, sulfur metabolism, methane cycling, or DNA repair. Record the dominant biological themes inferred from the refined SAGs.

Primary inferred role of the archaeal community in the extreme environment, such as biogeochemical cycling, primary production support, sulfur oxidation/reduction, or methanogenesis. Record the ecosystem-relevant interpretation generated from the final analysis.

Overall confidence score for the adaptation and ecosystem-function inference, derived from the comparative analysis output. Use the score scale defined by the analysis workflow; record the final confidence value for the derivative result.

Overall quality assessment of the final analytical result based on completeness of supporting evidence, consistency of annotations, and robustness of inference. Use this coarse flag to indicate whether the result set is high, medium, low, or failed quality.
